I've been farming this land for over 50 years, same as my father before me. Quzhou soil knows wheat and corn — that's what we grow here on the North China Plain, always has been. Two crops a year, wheat in winter, corn in summer, same fields rotating. I don't need anyone to tell me this. It's what works and what I know how to do.

My legs aren't what they used to be and my son is working in Shijiazhuang now. I hire the village machine cooperative for planting and harvesting — costs me a couple hundred yuan but I can manage the rest myself. I have about 10 mu total.

For wheat, I'll use the improved variety the village co-op sells, Jimai or whatever they have this year. Better than the old seed my father used. I put in fertilizer at sowing — diammonium phosphate and urea — and top-dress with urea in spring at jointing. Water is the problem here. No rain in spring so I pump from the well three times: once before sowing to settle the soil, once at jointing in April, once at heading in May. Costs me electricity but wheat without water is nothing. I spray twice — once for rust and powdery mildew after winter, once for aphids in May.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid corn immediately in the same fields. Zhengdan 958 — everyone around here uses it, reliable. No-till, straight into the stubble. Rain usually comes in July and August so I might only water once if it's dry. Corn has fewer worries but I spray once for borer.

I keep it simple. No experiments, no new crops. I'm 65. I know what this land gives me.
